$comment: The voice-over: one take per scene. `text` is the line as WRITTEN ("17 weeks", "example.com"); the brand's pronunciation lexicon (brand-tokens.json brand.pronunciations) turns it into what the voice is sent, and the captions show the written forms. A take may instead give `speak`, sent exactly as written. Each take starts at `at` and must finish before `until`, in FILM seconds (after inserts). `scene` says what is on screen; `anchors` are words that should land while their picture shows (reported by npm run narrate, not enforced). `verify` sets the listening check (speech-to-text): the most word error a take may have and how many times to re-voice a take that fails. `timing` is 'tts' (the voice's own timestamps) or 'forced-alignment' (re-aligned against the text). The narrator comes from brand-tokens.json video.voice.narrator; `voice` here is only the fallback. `auditions` lists voices for npm run audition. Eleven v3/v4 reject a seed, so seed is null. `recording` (optional): a voice-over a person read, {"file": "recordings/vo.m4a", "maxPause": 0.3, "speaker": "…"}; npm run narrate then cuts each take out of it instead of voicing it (references/sound.md). A take's `chapter` (optional) names a chapter in out/<basename>.publish.json; `clips` (optional) names the clips.json footage it shows.
